correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs the exact one-sided finite-difference perturbation, computes its Haar covariance from 15 sixth-moment pairings, applies Cauchy--Schwarz to each spectral two-step noise, constructs a simultaneously attaining spectral orthogonal reflection, and sums independent centered blocks at all finite even horizons. Strict spectral stability gives unique even-chain stationary law. All rational identities and supplementary Haar simulations passed the shipped Python checker. The result makes no finite-testing-to-infinite-proof leap; cross-block dependence and noisy functions are excluded.

value.rationale: The motivating structured zeroth-order algorithm leaves tailored quadratic analysis open, and persistent forward-difference noise matters even for a full orthogonal frame. The theorem completely determines the exact best stationary risk against every Haar-marginal within-block coupling, modewise and simultaneously, with a nontrivial sign-change frontier and mixed-sign counterexample to uniform-frame pairing. This is a mathematical coupling benchmark even though Hessian spectral information may make the attaining design costly in practice.
